name: Nergal
title: Babylonian idol worshipped in Samaria
summary: Nergal was a Mesopotamian deity associated with war, plague, and the underworld, worshipped by the people from Kut who were settled in Samaria by the Assyrian king after Israel's fall. He is mentioned in the Bible as one of the foreign gods introduced into the territory of the northern kingdom, illustrating the religious syncretism that characterized the region after the exile. In a biblical context, Nergal represents the threat of idolatry to the worship of the true God.

keyEvents.title: Assyrian deportation and resettlement in Samaria
keyEvents.description: After the Assyrian king conquered Samaria, people from several nations, including Kut, were settled in the cities of Samaria. The people from Kut brought with them the worship of Nergal.

keyEvents.title: Foreign gods in Samaria
keyEvents.description: Each nation that was settled in Samaria made their own images of gods and set them up in the high places. The people from Kut made Nergal as their deity.

keyEvents.title: Religious syncretism in Samaria
keyEvents.description: The newly arrived peoples feared the Lord while also serving their own gods, leading to a mixture of true worship and idolatry in the region of Samaria.

keyEvents.title: Persistent idolatry
keyEvents.description: Even though an Israelite priest was sent back to teach the peoples how to worship the Lord, they continued to worship their own gods, including Nergal, alongside the Lord.
